subject: Competitive bake-off recap: Omnitek evaluation
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sana Patel <sana.patel@omnitek.com>, Jorge Ruiz <jorge.ruiz@omnitek.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 15:02:00 -0400
Subject: Post-call recap: Omnitek / Redwood competitive bake-off

Hi Sana / Jorge — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so the team is aligned and we have clear next steps.

Pain points you shared:
- High per-token costs and unpredictable tail latency on peak inference traffic (mobile app peak at 5–6 PM ET).
- Existing vendor struggles with multi-region routing and data residency requirements for EU customers.
- Need for better observability to correlate cost vs. quality for A/B model variants.

Goals and decision criteria:
1) Latency: p95 under 400ms for short-chat flows (<= 256 tokens).
2) Cost: measurable unit-cost reduction vs incumbent at 6 months.
3) Reliability: multi-region failover and SLA for paid tier.
4) Privacy/compliance: support for customer-managed keys and audit logs.
5) Ease of integration: SDKs + migration playbook.

Competitive bake-off plan (proposed):
- Round 1 (this week): baseline throughput/latency tests against 1000 synthetic sessions (we'll run from our US and EU regions).
- Round 2 (next week): quality evaluation on your 250-sample prompt set and two persona scenarios.
- Scorecard: we attached a scorecard template (omnitek-bakeoff-scorecard.xlsx) — please fill the columns you own (security, procurement, product) and return by Friday.

Open questions we flagged during the call:
- Which model is your incumbent using in production (name + quantization)?
- Any strict compliance timeline for EU deployment?
- Will procurement want a standard SOW or PO-first approach?

Next concrete steps:
1) I will share the scorecard + test harness and schedule the first performance run from our side (target Thu).
2) Sana/Jorge: please confirm the incumbent model name and share the 250-sample prompt set.
3) Rishi/Neha: prep a lightweight config for quantized load tests and confirm target instance sizes.

Attachments: omnitek-bakeoff-scorecard.xlsx

Thanks — speak soon.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
(415) 555-0187

Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 10:20:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Omnitek / Redwood competitive bake-off

Marissa — thanks for the clear summary. Quick answers: we currently run an open-source variant (gpt-3.5-onnx quantized to 4-bit) for the bulk of traffic; a small subset uses vendor X for hallucination-sensitive flows.

I've asked procurement to loop in procurement@omnitek.com for PO questions — CC'd them on the separate thread. Attaching the 250-sample prompt set here (sent on shared Drive link) and we will populate the scorecard by EOD Friday.

One clarification on the test harness: can you run the synthetic sessions from both our US and Dublin endpoints? We need region parity.

Best,
Sana Patel
Senior Product Manager | Omnitek

Marissa / Neha — quick internal note after Sana's reply.

I validated the test harness and have the following proposal:
- We will run baseline perf from our us-east-1 and eu-west-1 clusters to match Omnitek endpoints.
- Use model variant: redwood-phi-7b (8-bit quant) as our primary test; run an additional quantized path (4-bit) to compare cost/quality tradeoffs.
- For fairness, throttle to match Omnitek's reported concurrency (30 concurrent sessions).

Open operational asks for Neha:
- Can you provision a short-lived EU test tenant with customer-managed KMS so we can demonstrate audit logs? Need creds by Tue EOD.
- Also capture token-level breakdown in trace for the scorecard.

I'll prepare the perf run scripts and push results to the scorecard link. Marissa — once Sana confirms test windows, I'll schedule runs.

-Rishi
